newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees volatile wheat markets amid low stocks.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees volatile wheat markets amid low stocks.

text.p: Low stocks of world wheat are likely to result in volatile markets over the next two years, the Economist Intelligence Unit said.
In its World Commodity Forecasts publication for the first quarter of 1997, the EIU says stocks are too low to ensure supplies in the event of crop failures or unexpected import demand.
"Prices will be vulnerable to market rumours and prone to sudden changes," the EIU said.
The EIU expects fob Gulf prices for US hard winter wheat to range between $180 and $190 per tonne until early 1999.

If there are simultaneous bumper harvests in the main exporting countries prices could slide to around $150 per tonne, but if one of them suffered a major crop failure in summer 1997 prices could again rise to well over $200 per tonne, the EIU said.
The EIU does not expect subsidy competition to re-emerge on a large scale in 1997 or 1998.
